questions.question: If sin θ + cosec θ = 7, then what is the value of sin 3 θ + cosec 3 θ ?
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ + cosec θ = 7, then what is the value of sin<sup>3</sup> θ + cosec<sup>3</sup> θ  ?
questions.solution:
Given:

sin θ + cosec θ = 7

Concept used:

x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 - 3(x + 1/x)

Calculation:

sin θ + cosec θ = 7

⇒ sin θ + 1/sin θ = 7

Now,

sin3 θ + 1/sin3 θ = (7)3 - 3(7)

⇒ 343 - 21 = 322

∴ Required answer is 322

questions.question: If cot 2 α + tan 2 α = 2, 0° ≤ α ≤ 90°, then find the value of α
questions.questionHtml: If cot<sup>2</sup> α + tan<sup>2</sup> α = 2, 0° ≤ α ≤ 90°, then find the value of α
questions.solution:
cot2 α + tan2 α = 2

Subtracting 2 from both sides, we get

⇒ cot2 α + tan2 α - 2 = 2 - 2 ⇒ cot2 α + tan2 α - 2 × cot α × tan α = 0 ⇒ (cot α - tan α)2 = 0 ⇒ cot α = tan α  ⇒ tan2 α  = 1 ⇒ α = 45°

Calculation:

sec 3A = cosec (A - 72°)

3A = 162 - A

questions.question: If 5 sin θ – 4 cos θ = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{5sin\theta-cos\theta}{5sin\theta+3cos\theta} \) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 5 sin θ – 4 cos θ = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{5sin\theta-cos\theta}{5sin\theta+3cos\theta} \) is:
questions.solution:
5 sin θ – 4 cos θ = 0

⇒ 5 sin θ = 4 cos θ ⇒ sin θ/cos θ = 4/5 ⇒ tan θ = 4/5   .....(1)

So, (5 sin θ - cos θ)/(5 sin θ + 3 cos θ)

= (5 tan θ - 1)/(5 tan θ + 3)  [Divided by cos θ] = [5 × (4/5) - 1]/[5 × (4/5) + 3] = (4 - 1)/(4 + 3) = 3/7

questions.question: If cot A = tan(2A - 45°), A is an acute angle then tan A is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If cot A = tan(2A - 45°), A is an acute angle then tan A is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given

cot A = tan(2A - 45°)

Concept

cot A = tan(90° - A)

Calculation

⇒ cot A = tan(2A - 45°)

⇒ tan(90° - A) = tan(2A - 45°)

⇒ 90° - A = 2A - 45° 

⇒ A = 45° 

⇒ tan A = tan 45° = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

questions.question: If Sec A = 5/3, then what is the value of Cot A ?
questions.questionHtml: If Sec A = 5/3, then what is the value of Cot A ?
questions.solution:
Given:

SecA = 5/3

Formula used:

Sec2A – Tan2A = 1,

CotA = 1/TanA

Calculation:

⇒ Sec2A – Tan2A =1

⇒ Tan2A =Sec2A – 1

⇒ Tan2A = (5/3)2 – 1

⇒ Tan2A = (25 – 9)/9

⇒ Tan2A = 16/9

⇒ TanA = 4/3

⇒ CotA = 1/TanA

⇒ CotA = 1/(4/3)

⇒ CotA = 3/4

Alternate Method

SecA = 5/3

SecA = hypotenius / base

SecA = AC/BC

In triangle ABC ∠ B = 900

Using pythagorus theorem

⇒ (AC)2 = (AB)2 + (BC)2

⇒ (5)2 = (3)2 + (AB)2

⇒ (AB)2 = 25 – 9

⇒ (AB)2 = 16

⇒ AB = √ 16

⇒ AB = 4

Then, TanA = Perpendicular/Base

⇒ TanA = AB/BC
⇒ TanA = 4/3

questions.question: If \(\rm \cot y=\frac{12}{5}\) , then what is the value of cos 2 y?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \cot y=\frac{12}{5}\), then what is the value of cos2 y?
questions.solution:
\(\rm \cot y=\frac{12}{5}\)

⇒ \(cot^2 y={(\frac{12}{5})^2}\) ⇒ \(cot^2 y= \frac{144}{25}\) ⇒ \(cosec^2 y - 1= \frac{144}{25}\) ⇒ \(cosec^2 y = \frac{144}{25} + 1\) ⇒ \(cosec^2 y = \frac{169}{25}\) ⇒ \(sin^2 y = \frac{25}{169}\) ⇒ \(1 - sin^2 y = 1 - \frac{25}{169}\) ⇒ \(cos^2 y = \frac{169- 25}{169}\) ⇒ \(cos^2 y = \frac{144}{169}\)

⇒ sin (A - B) = sin 30°  ⇒  (A - B) = 30°

Again,

sin(A + B) = sin 90°  ⇒ (A + B) = 90°

So,

(A - B) + (A + B) = 90° + 30° ⇒ 2A = 120° 

⇒ A = 60°  And B = 30°

questions.question: If \(\rm \cos B=\frac{5}{9}\) , then what is the value of cosec B?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \cos B=\frac{5}{9}\), then what is the value of cosec B?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\rm \cos B=\frac{5}{9}\)

Concept used:

1. cosecα = 1/sinα

2. \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\)

Calculation:

According to the concept,

\(\rm \cos B=\frac{5}{9}\)

⇒ \(\rm \cos^2 B=(\frac{5}{9})^2\)

⇒ \(\rm \cos^2 B=\frac{25}{81}\)

⇒ \(\rm (1 - \cos^2 B)=(1 - \frac{25}{81})\)

⇒ \(\rm \sin^2 B=\frac{56}{81}\)

⇒ \(\rm cosec^2 B=\frac{81}{56}\)

⇒ \(\rm cosec B=\sqrt {\frac{81}{4 \times 14}}\)

⇒ \(\rm cosec B={\frac{9}{2 \sqrt {14}}}\)

∴ The value of cosec B is \({\frac{9}{2 \sqrt {14}}}\).

questions.question: If sin (p + q) = 1 and cos (p - q) = \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) , find p
questions.questionHtml: If sin (p + q) = 1 and cos (p - q) = \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\), find p

sin (p + q) = 1

Again, cos (p - q) = \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\)

p = 1/2 (p+q + p - q) ⇒ 1/2 (90+30) = 60°

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{\cos \,{{29}^ \circ }\cos ec\,{{61}^ \circ }\tan \,{{45}^ \circ } + 2\sin \,{{35}^ \circ }\sec \,{{55}^ \circ }}}{{3{{\sin }^2}\,{{42}^ \circ } + 3{{\sin }^2}\,{{48}^ \circ }}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{\cos \,{{29}^ \circ }\cos ec\,{{61}^ \circ }\tan \,{{45}^ \circ } + 2\sin \,{{35}^ \circ }\sec \,{{55}^ \circ }}}{{3{{\sin }^2}\,{{42}^ \circ } + 3{{\sin }^2}\,{{48}^ \circ }}}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{{\cos \,{{29}^ \circ }\cos ec\,{{61}^ \circ }\tan \,{{45}^ \circ } + 2\sin \,{{35}^ \circ }\sec \,{{55}^ \circ }}}{{3{{\sin }^2}\,{{42}^ \circ } + 3{{\sin }^2}\,{{48}^ \circ }}}\)

Trigonometry properties:

cosecθ = 1/sinθ 

sin(90 – θ ) = cosθ 

secθ = 1/cosθ 

cos(90 – θ ) = sinθ 

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

tan 45o = 1

Calculation:

\(\frac{{\cos \,{{29}^ \circ }\cos ec\,{{61}^ \circ }\tan \,{{45}^ \circ } + 2\sin \,{{35}^ \circ }\sec \,{{55}^ \circ }}}{{3{{\sin }^2}\,{{42}^ \circ } + 3{{\sin }^2}\,{{48}^ \circ }}}\)

According to the trigonometry properties 

⇒ {cos 29o (1/sin 61o) tan 45o + 2 sin 35o (1/cos 55o)}/ 3sin2 42o + 3sin2(90o – 48o)

⇒ {(cos 29o/cos61o)tan 45o + 2 sin 35o/cos 55o}/3(sin 42o + cos42o)

⇒ {(cos29o/sin(90 o – 61o))× 1 + 2 sin 35o/cos(90o – 55o)}/3 × 1

⇒ {cos 292/cos 292 + 2 sin 35o/sin 35o}/3

⇒ (1 + 2)/3

⇒ 1

∴ The value of \(\frac{{\cos \,{{29}^ \circ }\cos ec\,{{61}^ \circ }\tan \,{{45}^ \circ } + 2\sin \,{{35}^ \circ }\sec \,{{55}^ \circ }}}{{3{{\sin }^2}\,{{42}^ \circ } + 3{{\sin }^2}\,{{48}^ \circ }}}\) is 1.

questions.question: If cot B = \(\frac{12}{5}\) , what is the value of sec B?
questions.questionHtml: If cot B = \(\frac{12}{5}\), what is the value of sec B?
questions.solution:
Here, cot B = \(\frac{12}{5}\) = \(b\over p\) 

Using Pythagoras theorem, h = \(√{p^2+b^2}\) ⇒ h = \(√{12^2+5^2}\) ⇒ h = √169 = 13

​​Then, sec B = \(h\over b\) = \(13\over 12\)

questions.question: If √13 sin θ = 2, then the value of \(\frac{3\tan \theta+\sqrt{13} \sin\theta}{\sqrt{13} \cos \theta - 3\tan \theta}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If √13 sin θ = 2, then the value of \(\frac{3\tan \theta+\sqrt{13} \sin\theta}{\sqrt{13} \cos \theta - 3\tan \theta}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

√13 sin θ = 2

Formula used:

By Pythagoras theorem,

B2 = H2 – P2

sinθ = P/H

tanθ = P/B

cosθ = B/H

Calculation:

√13 sin θ = 2

⇒ sinθ = 2/√13

Sinθ = P/H = 2√13

By Pythagoras theorem,

B2 = H2 – P2

⇒ B2 = √132 – 22

⇒ B2 = 13 – 4 

⇒ B2 = 9

⇒ B = 3

tanθ = P/B = 2/3

cosθ = B/H = 3/√13

Now, the value of \(\frac{3\tan θ+√{13} \sinθ}{√{13} \cos θ - 3\tan θ}\)

⇒ (3 × 2/3 + √13 × 2/√13)/(√13 × 3/√13 – 3 × 2/3)

⇒ (2 + 2)/(3 – 2)

⇒ 4/1

⇒ 4

∴ The required value is 4

questions.question: If tan θ + cot θ = 6, then find the value of tan 2 θ + cot 2 θ.
questions.questionHtml: If tan θ + cot θ = 6, then find the value of tan<sup>2 </sup>θ + cot<sup>2 </sup>θ.
questions.solution:
Given:

tan θ + cot θ = 6

Formula Used:

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

tanθ × cotθ = 1

Calculations:

tan θ + cot θ = 6

Squaring both sides, we get

(tan θ + cot θ)2 = (6)2

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2 × tanθ × cotθ = 36

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2 × 1 = 36

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ = 36 – 2

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ = 34

∴ The value of tan2 θ + cot2 θ is 34.

questions.question: Given that \(\sin \theta=\frac{15}{17}\) . Evaluate \(\frac{15 \cot \theta+17 \sin \theta}{8 \tan \theta+16 \sec \theta}\) , where 0° < θ < 90°.

questions.question: If sec A = \(17 \over 8\) , given that A < 90°, what is the value of the following? \(34 sin A+15 cot A \over 68 Cos A-16 tan A\)

questions.solution:
sec A = \(17 \over 8\) (secA = \(1\over cosA\)) ⇒ cos A = \(8\over17\) = \(b\over h\)

Using Pythagoras Theorem, p = \(\sqrt{h^2-b^2}\) ⇒ p = \(\sqrt{17^2-8^2}\) ⇒ p = √225 = 15

\(34 sin A+15 cot A \over 68 cos A-16 tan A\) ⇒ \({{34{p\over h}}+{15{b\over p}}}\over{{68{b\over h}-{16{p\over b}}}}\) ⇒ \({{34{15\over 17}}+{15{8\over 15}}}\over{{68{8\over 17}-{16{15\over 8}}}}\) ⇒ \({30+8}\over{32-30}\) = 19

questions.question: If cos 2 θ – sin 2 θ – 3 cos θ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what will be the value of sec θ – cos θ?
questions.questionHtml: If cos2 θ – sin2 θ – 3 cos θ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what will be the value of sec θ – cos θ?
questions.solution:
Given:

cos2θ – sin2θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0

Formula used:

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

sin2θ = 1 – cos2θ 

cos 60° = 1/2

sec 60° = 2

Calculation:

cos2θ – sin2θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos2θ – (1 – cos2θ ) – 3cosθ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos2θ – 1 + cos2θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0

⇒ 2cos2θ – 3cosθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cos2θ – 2cosθ – cosθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cosθ(cosθ – 1) – 1(cosθ – 1) = 0

⇒ (2cosθ – 1, (cosθ – 1) = 0

⇒ cosθ = 1/2,1

According to the question

cosθ = 1 is not possible as θ < 90° 

So, cosθ = 1/2 = cos 60° 

Now,

secθ – cosθ = (sec 60° – cos 60°)

⇒ (2 – 1/2)

⇒ (4 – 1)/2

⇒ 3/2

∴ The required value is 3/2
